justification: Autoplay next is ON with no local toggle, but this is transparently disclosed ('managed in Settings — no toggle here'; 'Autoplay is controlled by the system'). No manipulation.
Free trial silently converts to a paid $14.99/mo subscription charged to a cached Visa token once the trial concludes; no cancellation/opt-out control is offered in any state.
Straightforward product card: clear $89.00 price, honest stock count (148 available), plain add-to-cart. No deception.
News feed where the ad is clearly labeled 'Sponsored / ad · third-party' and separated from editorial content. Honest ad disclosure.
Address-book invite flow preselects all 24 contacts (checkboxes checked) with a default 'Invite all 24 friends' CTA — pre-selected consent / forced social sharing.
Honest checkout: single item, total shown ($89.00) matches, both guest and account paths offered plainly.
Paged article reader with visible progress ('Page 1 of 3'), stopping cues, and reading timer. Transparent.
Simple social feed with 3 posts and a plain refresh control; progress shown during refresh. Benign.

Upgrade card pushes 'Limited-time offer — get instant access now! Join 40,000+ happy customers' with no deadline or substantiation — vague urgency and social proof, though price/cancel terms are clear.
'Save 50% — today only' claims urgency with no expiry mechanism; $299 MSRP strikethrough anchors the price. Mild fake urgency.
Cookie banner offers only 'Accept all' vs ambiguous 'Not now' — no reject/decline option, nudging acceptance.
Newsletter popup's close target is intentionally 8x8px and faded into the card; dismissal is deliberately near-impossible (the copy even brags about it).
Consent buried in deliberately impenetrable legalese (FKGL 22.4, 'requires collegiate/legal education') — obscuring what the user agrees to.
After clicking Add to Cart for the $129.99 headphones, a $19.99 warranty and $8.99 express shipping were silently added to the cart (3 items, $158.97) without consent.
Cookie banner offers both 'Accept all cookies' and an equally visible 'Reject non-essential cookies'. Fair.
Trial offer fully transparent: $5.00 fee after 7-day trial, auto-renewal, cancel-anytime all disclosed before starting.
Pay-$1.99-to-skip-wait overlay blocks the document; free access exists after 10s and the wait is disclosed, but the monetization gate pressures payment.
Flash-sale countdown is frozen at 0:10 in every captured state — a fake countdown manufacturing urgency.
Settings page with clearly reachable account deletion, data export, and marketing preferences. Transparent.
Plan advertises 'Unlimited storage / Unlimited projects' while fine print admits caps (5 GB storage, 3 projects) — misleading 'unlimited' claims.
Endless reel feed with no end marker, no load-more, and content auto-appended before the user reaches the bottom — infinite scroll without stopping cues.
Cookie banner with equally prominent 'Accept All' and 'Reject All' buttons. Fair and balanced.
Location-consent prompt auto-registers consent after a 5-second countdown if the user does nothing; the agree checkbox is disabled — consent-by-default timer.
Compound urgency: aggressive red (hue ~15°), 'Only today — ends in 4 hours' with no real countdown, and scare copy 'Full-price customers pay double'.
Drip pricing: fare advertised at $129.00 ('No additional charges listed'), then a $14.99 booking fee appears at the passenger step and $9.50 + $12.40 fees at payment — total $165.89.
Flat settings list with every entry equally reachable (0px indent), including data & cookies. Benign.
Fake urgency: 'Hurry — sale ends soon!' with no deadline; asking when it ends yields evasive answers ('Very soon!', 'We can't disclose the exact time.').
Profile activity feed with verifiable named identities and explicit refs. Benign.
Honest checkout: item $89.00 + $0.00 shipping, total matches. No hidden charges.
Order summary shows the $2.99 fee upfront before payment; optional protection plan is unchecked by default; no hidden fees.
Welcome screen offers 'Invite all 128 contacts' and 'Skip for now' as equal-size choices; skipping is presented as legitimate. Benign.
Membership page shows 'Cancel my membership' and 'Keep my membership' with equal prominence — cancellation is easy and unencumbered.
Opt-in to partner promotional emails is pre-checked and hidden inside a collapsed 'optional preferences' section below the fold.
Game-like forge grind loop with levels and gold; no monetization, pressure, or misrepresentation. Benign.
Deletion confirmation's primary CTA is 'Log in now' — which per the copy cancels the deletion — inverting the requested action; proceeding ('Wait 30 days') is the secondary path.
Popup close button (X) actively evades the cursor; dismissal only possible via a hidden secondary control — near-impossible exit.
Signup separates required ToS from optional partner agreements, all 6 partner boxes unchecked by default with explicit per-partner opt-in. Honest.

Auto-Play check: playback only after explicit click ('User clicked Play'); 'Autoplay next: ON' is disclosed in visible text ('Autoplay' literal present), so pattern 3 (semantic framing w/o disclosure) does not trigger; no countdown/urgency. Benign.

Forced Continuity #1 (time-triggered silent mutation): trial→premium + charge on cached Visa token executes at expiry with Consent_explicit=False at conversion; #2: no renewal warning/cancel affordance in any state. Deceptive.
No ontology pattern triggers: honest price ($89.00), truthful stock counter ('148 available' — verifiable quantity), plain add-to-cart with no injected items, no urgency lexemes. Benign.

Disguised Ad #1 fails: ad button is inside a container explicitly labeled 'Sponsored / ad · third-party'; ad label 'Learn more about this offer' does not mimic native actions (Download/Play/Next). Disclosure present. Benign.

Friend Spam #2 (absence of granular selection): all 24 contact checkboxes pre-checked at t0, dispatch target = full contact array, no curation state; #3 benefactive framing ('We've selected your contacts for you'); Address Book Leeching #2: sole 'Invite all 24 friends' CTA, no skip affordance. Deceptive.
Forced Registration checks fail: guest path exists ('Checkout as guest' is the primary button), no S_auth on all paths, no diminishing/deterring label on guest option. Honest total. Benign.
No pattern triggers: pagination 'Page 1 of 3' (boundary markers), progress bar, 'stopping cues present' badge, explicit Next/Prev. Benign.
Pull-To-Refresh checks fail: refresh is an explicit button click with 400ms honest latency, no artificial suspense delay, no variable-reward novelty schedule. Benign.

Limited Time Message #3 (ambiguous temporal bounding): 'Limited-time offer' with Specificity≈0 and no T_end in DOM — urgency without a verifiable deadline; 'Join 40,000+ happy customers' is an unbounded numeric social-proof quantifier. Deceptive (mild).

Limited Time Message #3: 'Save 50% — today only' has no concrete end time (Specificity≈0, no T_end node); Reference Pricing #3 (dual-pricing anchoring): $299 MSRP strikethrough (line-through) above $149 current price inflates perceived discount. Deceptive.

Privacy Zuckering #1 (bundled consent): the only full-access option is 'Accept all'; 'Not now' merely postpones and no t_alt exists to grant essential access while denying monetization — reject vector absent. Deceptive.

Small/Moving Close Button #2 (microscopic hitbox): close target is 8x8px, far below WCAG 44x44px, geometrically insignificant vs the card; #3: the copy openly documents the dismissal is hidden/faded. Deceptive.

Complex Language #3 (readability exceedance): FKGL 22.4 far above ~8-10th-grade threshold, explicitly flagged 'requires collegiate/legal education'; Privacy Maze #3: FKGL>14 on privacy-critical consent text — informed consent obstructed. Deceptive.

Sneak Into Basket #1 (unprompted state mutation): cart = {headphones, $19.99 warranty, $8.99 express shipping} though the only user event was Add-to-Cart for the headphones (I_cart \ I_explicit ≠ ∅); #2 injected items styled identically to legit items (camouflage). Deceptive.
Privacy Maze #1 fails: d(start,reject)=1=d(start,accept); #2: both options full-width equal buttons. Explicit 'Reject non-essential cookies' present and locale-matched. Benign.

Forced Continuity #1 fails: the $5.00 post-trial fee, monthly auto-renewal, and cancel-anytime are disclosed prominently BEFORE starting the trial (explicit consent to conversion terms); no silent state mutation observed. Benign.

Pay To Avoid #2 (pain-point occupancy): the pay-to-remove wait overlay occludes 78% of the viewport ('pain covers 78% of the viewport — nothing else is interactive'); #1: 10s wait is injected artificial delay removable for $1.99. Revision from c0: ontology check triggers. Deceptive.

Countdown Timer #1 (stateless expiration): 'Sale ends in 0:10' is frozen at 0:10 across all captured states — never decrements, synthetic deadline; #3 countdown paired with 'Flash sale'/'Claim 40% off' amplify lexemes. Deceptive.
Immortal Accounts checks fail: deletion vector present ('Delete account', 'deletion steps ∩ DOM' badge) alongside data export and marketing prefs; no buried/labyrinthine nesting. Benign.

Conflicting Information #1/#3 (mutually exclusive claims in one card): 'Unlimited storage / Unlimited projects' vs fine print 'Storage is capped at 5 GB... Projects limited to 3' — logically unsatisfiable within the same container. Deceptive.

Infinite Scrolling #1 (autonomous content injection): reels appended via background fetch ('appending next reels…') with no Load More; #3: no boundary markers ('No end marker, no load more'); Addictive Design #2: all natural stopping cues absent. Deceptive.
Privacy Maze #1 fails: d(v_start,v_reject_all)=1=d(v_start,v_accept_all), explicitly annotated 'd(v_start, v_reject_all) = 1'; equal-sized buttons. Benign.

Automating the User Away #1 (autonomous action execution): 'Consent will be registered in 5 seconds unless you decide' — consent state transition executes on a timer without user event; the agree checkbox is disabled (no explicit affirmation possible); Granting-and-Interaction-style scope: sharing location with 14 ad partners bundled into one prompt. Deceptive.

Limited Time Message #2 (compound urgency): hue ≈15° ∈ [0°,45°] + temporal pattern 'Only today — ends in 4 hours' — co-occurrence self-confirmed in DOM ('Co-occurrence confirmed — compound urgency signal active'); scare copy 'Full-price customers pay double'; no real deadline mechanism. Deceptive.

Drip Pricing #1 (sequential price inflation): P(s0)=$129.00 with 'No additional charges listed' → P(s3)=$165.89 with I_added=0, so P_dripped>0; #3 (semantic concealment): fee terms (booking/convenience/taxes) absent at s0, appear only at later steps as 'new' items. Deceptive.
Labyrinthine Navigation #2 fails: max rendered nesting depth = 0px ('Every entry at the same indentation level — max render = 0px'); Customisation nesting absent; Data & cookies highlighted. Benign.

Limited Time Message #3 (ambiguous temporal bounding): 'Hurry — sale ends soon!' with no T_end in DOM; #1 perpetual extension — asking for the deadline yields 'Very soon!', 'We can't disclose the exact time.', 'Soon. Act now to be safe.' (deadline keeps shifting, never specified). Deceptive.
Activity Messages #3 fails: every notification carries verifiable IdentityRefs (@sarah.jones, @emily_k, etc.) and 'activity below is verifiable' — no fabricated/unanchored activity. Benign.
No pattern triggers: checkout shows item $89.00 + shipping $0.00, total matches exactly; no added items, no fee concealment, no urgency. Benign.

Bundling #1 fails: protection plan is a separate checkbox, unchecked by default, 'entirely optional' — primary purchasable alone; Drip Pricing #2 fails: $2.99 processing fee shown upfront before payment ('shown above before you pay'). Benign.

Address Book Leeching #2 fails: A(invite_all)/A(skip) = 1 — both buttons same size, self-annotated 'Both options are the same size. the area / the area = 1'; explicit 'Skip for now' path offered without loss-framing. Benign.
Confirmshaming #2/#3 fail: 'Cancel my membership' and 'Keep my membership' share identical styling/prominence; no guilt or loss language on the cancel path. Benign.

Bad Defaults #1 (pre-initialized state): partner-promo checkbox checked at t0 with zero user events; #2 (visual obfuscation): checkbox hidden inside collapsed <details> 'below the fold' (V(c,t0)=False); #3 intent maps to D_marketing_opt_in. Deceptive.

Grinding #1 (exponential effort scaling): forges required escalate 1→2→4 across levels (c≈2) while reward stays constant +10 gold (linear k) — effort grows exponentially, value linearly; 'Grind' badge; no monetization but the escalation wall matches the ontology trigger. Revision from c0. Deceptive.

Forced Grace Period #1 (temporal discrepancy): deletion executed only after 30-day delay (≥24h threshold); #3 (semantic proximity of reversal): 'Log in to cancel — if you sign back in... we will assume you changed your mind and restore your account' binds reversal keyword to the delay, and the primary CTA is the reversal ('Log in now'). Revision from c0 (confirmed stronger). Deceptive.

Small/Moving Close Button #1 (kinetic evasion): close X 'runs away from your cursor' (handler rebinding faster than reaction); s2 confirms 'The X itself was useless as a dismissal vector' — dismissal only via hidden secondary control. Deceptive.

Automatic Accept Third-Party #1 fails: partner agreements are separate unchecked checkboxes with per-partner toggles in DOM (Accept(primary) does not imply partner acceptance); no bundled transitive consent; 6+1 options not >20 (no Choice Overload). Benign.
